summary: The customer wants to know which technical parameters to clarify and what an initial comparison experiment should establish to evaluate a remote, fiber-coupled optical measurement of water in a petroleum stream.

facts_stated.text: The process handles a petroleum stream.
Samples are currently sent to a laboratory for water determination.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: currently send samples to a laboratory for water determination

facts_stated.text: The analyzer would be situated outside the process area.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: The analyzer would be outside the process area

targets.purpose: noticing changes sooner by measuring closer to the process

process.value: laboratory water determination on discrete samples
process.enquiry_quote: send samples to a laboratory for water determination

process.value: analyzer located outside the process area
process.enquiry_quote: The analyzer would be outside the process area

process.value: measurement positioned closer to the process
faster detection of changes than sending samples to the lab
process.enquiry_quote: so that changes can be noticed sooner

unknowns: Expected water concentration range, target detection limit, and required precision/accuracy
Stream physical state (liquid, gas, multiphase) and composition (e.g., crude oil, refined hydrocarbon, condensate)
Optical properties of the stream (transparency, turbidity, scattering, color, emulsion state, suspended solids)
Process operating conditions: line temperature, pressure, and flow velocity/variability
Physical distance between the measurement point and the analyzer shelter/control room outside the process area
Hazardous area classification (e.g., ATEX/IECEx zone) at the probe installation point
Probe interface constraints, potential window fouling/coating, and cleaning access
Exact laboratory reference method used (e.g., Karl Fischer titration) and its typical turnaround time
